headline: UVM police investigate alleged drink-spiking reports in Burlington
dek: A Sept. 30 alert says the reports involve off-campus locations, a cash reward is available for information, and temporary weekend screening support will be offered to students in October.
body: University of Vermont Police Services is investigating reports that people may have been given incapacitating drugs without their knowledge at off-campus locations in Burlington, prompting a campus safety alert and a request for information from students and the broader community.

The Sept. 30 alert says UVM Police and Safety Teams received reports of alleged incapacitating or so-called date-rape drug incidents in the Burlington area. It does not identify the locations, disclose what substances may have been involved or say how many people reported incidents. The alert says criminal investigations are ongoing and that UVM is offering a substantial cash reward for information that leads to the apprehension of a suspect or suspects. Anyone with information is asked to call UVM Police at 802-656-3473. ([UVM Police alert](https://content.getrave.com/artifacts/api/v1/riki/alert/2645895/moreInfoFile/3e2e5059-d183-4ba2-a0d6-d4fc2bc6acd8))

Local reporting adds limited context but does not resolve those unknowns. [WCAX reported](https://www.wcax.com/2026/09/30/uvm-police-warn-drink-spiking-offer-reward-information/) that sources described three or four incidents at different locations. [WPTZ reported](https://www.mynbc5.com/article/uvm-police-investigate-alleged-date-rape-drug-incidents/73967944), citing UVM Chief Safety and Compliance Officer Michael Schirling, that officials believed the reports involved multiple distinct events, multiple people and more than one location. Those descriptions are part of an active investigation, not a court finding that a crime occurred in any particular case.

Burlington Police told WCAX they had not seen a trend of these incidents. That distinction matters: UVM’s alert is a warning about allegations under investigation, not a declaration that a citywide pattern has been established. The reports also concern off-campus places, so the alert reaches beyond the university’s property and asks anyone who may have information to come forward. UVM urged people attending parties or visiting bars and restaurants to avoid leaving drinks unattended, reject open drinks from others and seek help quickly if they feel suddenly weak, confused or otherwise unwell.

UVM’s existing [incapacitating-drug screening initiative](https://www.uvm.edu/dsc/incapacitating-drug-screening-initiative), operated with UVM Medical Center, is designed for students who believe they were drugged but do not necessarily suspect a sexual assault. The university says testing is most useful when obtained promptly because some substances leave the body quickly. The program says Student Health Services can provide screening, and that testing may be tracked anonymously on request. If sexual assault is suspected, UVM directs people to the UVM Medical Center Emergency Department for examination and treatment.

The new alert adds a short-term change for October: weekend on-call support will be available for screening, giving students an option besides going directly to an emergency department. UVM says students can contact Police Services and be connected with a Student Health Services medical provider through the Center for Health and Well Being. The university also says reporting does not force a person into a full investigation; its screening guidance describes options ranging from a full report to sharing only basic timing and location information that may help investigators identify patterns.

The next steps are investigative. UVM Police are seeking tips, but the alert does not announce an arrest, identify a suspect or establish whether the allegations are connected. Students and community members who feel unsafe or witness a crime in progress should call 911; people seeking confidential support can contact Hope Works, which UVM lists as a 24-hour resource at 802-863-1236. Until investigators release more information, the confirmed public facts are the alert, the request for tips and the temporary screening support—not a confirmed count of victims or a proven explanation for what happened.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: UVM police investigate alleged drink-spiking reports in Burlington
seoDescription: UVM Police are investigating alleged off-campus drink-spiking incidents in Burlington and are offering a reward for information.
